munajat.ar: اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
munajat.tr: allahumma salli `ala muhammadin wa ali muhammadin
munajat.en: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad,

munajat.ar: وَٱسْمَعْ دُعَائِي إِذَا دَعَوْتُكَ
munajat.tr: wasma` du`a'i idha da`awtuka
munajat.en: and hear my supplication when I supplicate to You,

munajat.ar: وَٱسْمَعْ نِدَائِي إِذَا نَادَيْتُكَ
munajat.tr: wasma` nida'i idha nadaytuka
munajat.en: and hear my call when I call out to You,

munajat.ar: وَأَقْبِلْ عَلَيَّ إِذَا نَاجَيْتُكَ
munajat.tr: wa aqbil `alayya idha najaytuka
munajat.en: and turn towards me when I speak with You in private.

munajat.ar: فَقَدْ هَرَبْتُ إِلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: faqad harabtu ilayka
munajat.en: For I have fled to You,

munajat.ar: وَوَقَفْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ مُسْتَكِيناً لَكَ
munajat.tr: wa waqaftu bayna yadayka mustakinan laka
munajat.en: and I stand before You, humbled before You,

munajat.ar: مُتَضَرِّعاً إِلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: mutadarri`an ilayka
munajat.en: pleading with You,

munajat.ar: رَاجِياً لِمَا لَدَيْكَ ثَوَابِي
munajat.tr: rajiyan lima ladayka thawabi
munajat.en: hoping for the reward that is with You for me.

munajat.ar: وَتَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِي
munajat.tr: wa ta`lamu ma fi nafsi
munajat.en: You know what is within my soul,

munajat.ar: وَتَخْبُرُ حَاجَتِي
munajat.tr: wa takhburu hajati
munajat.en: You are fully aware of my need,

munajat.ar: وَتَعْرِفُ ضَمِيرِي
munajat.tr: wa ta`rifu damiri
munajat.en: and You know my innermost thoughts.

munajat.ar: وَلاَ يَخْفَىٰ عَلَيْكَ أَمْرُ مُنْقَلَبِي وَمَثْوَايَ
munajat.tr: wa la yakhfa `alayka amru munqalabi wa mathwaya
munajat.en: Nothing of my comings and goings, nor of my final resting place, is hidden from You,

munajat.ar: وَمَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُبْدِئَ بِهِ مِنْ مَنْطِقِي
munajat.tr: wa ma uridu an ubdi'a bihi min mantiqi
munajat.en: nor what I mean to begin saying,

munajat.ar: وَأَتَفَوَّهَ بِهِ مِنْ طَلِبَتِي
munajat.tr: wa atafawwaha bihi min talibati
munajat.en: nor the request I mean to put into words,

munajat.ar: وَأَرْجُوهُ لِعَاقِبَتِي
munajat.tr: wa arjuhu li`aqibati
munajat.en: nor what I hope for in my final outcome.

munajat.ar: وَقَدْ جَرَتْ مَقَادِيرُكَ عَلَيَّ يَا سَيِّدِي
munajat.tr: wa qad jarat maqadiruka `alayya ya sayyidi
munajat.en: Your decrees have already run their course over me, O my Master,

munajat.ar: فِيمَا يَكُونُ مِنِّي إِلَىٰ آخِرِ عُمْرِي
munajat.tr: fima yakunu minni ila akhiri `umri
munajat.en: in all that will come from me until the end of my life,

munajat.ar: مِنْ سَرِيرَتِي وَعَلانِيَتِي
munajat.tr: min sarirati wa `alaniyati
munajat.en: in what I keep secret and what I show openly.

munajat.ar: وَبِيَدِكَ لاَ بِيَدِ غَيْرِكَ زِيَادَتِي وَنَقْصِي
munajat.tr: wa biyadika la biyadi ghayrika ziyadati wa naqsi
munajat.en: In Your hand, and in no hand but Yours, lie my increase and my decrease,

munajat.ar: وَنَفْعِي وَضَرِّي
munajat.tr: wa naf`i wa darri
munajat.en: my benefit and my harm.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ حَرَمْتَنِي فَمَنْ ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرْزُقُنِي
munajat.tr: ilahi in haramtani faman dha alladhi yarzuquni
munajat.en: My God, if You deprive me, then who is there to provide for me?

munajat.ar: وَإِنْ خَذَلْتَنِي فَمَنْ ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَنْصُرُنِي
munajat.tr: wa in khadhaltani faman dha alladhi yansuruni
munajat.en: And if You abandon me, then who is there to help me?

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ غَضَبِكَ وَحُلُولِ سَخَطِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi a`udhu bika min ghadabika wa hululi sakhatika
munajat.en: My God, I seek refuge in You from Your anger and from Your displeasure coming down upon me.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ كُنْتُ غَيْرَ مُسْتَأْهِلٍ لِرَحْمَتِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in kuntu ghayra musta'hilin lirahmatika
munajat.en: My God, if I am not worthy of Your mercy,

munajat.ar: فَأَنْتَ أَهْلٌ أَنْ تَجُودَ عَلَيَّ بِفَضْلِ سَعَتِكَ
munajat.tr: fa-anta ahlun an tajuda `alayya bifadli sa`atika
munajat.en: You are worthy of being generous to me out of the bounty of Your vastness.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي كَأَنِّي بِنَفْسِي وَاقِفَةٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi ka-anni binafsi waqifatun bayna yadayka
munajat.en: My God, it is as if I see my soul standing before You,

munajat.ar: وَقَدْ أَظَلَّهَا حُسْنُ تَوَكُّلِي عَلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: wa qad azallaha husnu tawakkuli `alayka
munajat.en: shaded by the beauty of my trust in You,

munajat.ar: فَقُلْتَ مَا أَنْتَ أَهْلُهُ وَتَغَمَّدْتَنِي بِعَفْوِكَ
munajat.tr: faqulta ma anta ahluhu wa taghammadtani bi`afwika
munajat.en: and You have said what befits You and covered me over with Your pardon.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ عَفَوْتَ فَمَنْ أَوْلَىٰ مِنْكَ بِذٰلِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in `afawta faman awla minka bidhalika
munajat.en: My God, if You pardon, then who is more fitting than You to do so?

munajat.ar: وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ دَنَا أَجَلِي وَلَمْ يُدْنِنِي مِنْكَ عَمَلِي
munajat.tr: wa in kana qad dana ajali wa lam yudnini minka `amali
munajat.en: And if my appointed time has drawn near and my deeds have not drawn me near to You,

munajat.ar: فَقَدْ جَعَلْتُ ٱلإِقْرَارَ بِٱلذَّنْبِ إِلَيْكَ وَسِيلَتِي
munajat.tr: faqad ja`altu al-iqrara bildhdhanbi ilayka wasilati
munajat.en: then I have made my confession of my sin to You my means of approach.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي قَدْ جُرْتُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِي فِي ٱلنَّظَرِ لَهَا
munajat.tr: ilahi qad jurtu `ala nafsi fi alnnazari laha
munajat.en: My God, I have wronged my own soul in how I looked after it,

munajat.ar: فَلَهَا ٱلْوَيْلُ إِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَهَا
munajat.tr: falaha alwaylu in lam taghfir laha
munajat.en: so woe to it if You do not forgive it.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي لَمْ يَزَلْ بِرُّكَ عَلَيَّ أَيَّامَ حَيَاتِي
munajat.tr: ilahi lam yazal birruka `alayya ayyama hayati
munajat.en: My God, Your kindness towards me has never ceased in all the days of my life,

munajat.ar: فَلاَ تَقْطَعْ بِرَّكَ عَنِّي فِي مَمَاتِي
munajat.tr: fala taqta` birraka `anni fi mamati
munajat.en: so do not cut Your kindness off from me at my death.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي كَيفَ آيَسُ مِنْ حُسْنِ نَظَرِكَ لِي بَعْدَ مَمَاتِي
munajat.tr: ilahi kayfa ayasu min husni nazarika li ba`da mamati
munajat.en: My God, how could I despair of Your gracious regard for me after my death,

munajat.ar: وَأَنْتَ لَمْ تُوَلِّنِي إِلاَّ ٱلْجَمِيلَ فِي حَيَاتِي
munajat.tr: wa anta lam tuwallini illa aljamila fi hayati
munajat.en: when You have shown me nothing but beauty throughout my life?

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي تَوَلَّ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا أَنْتَ أَهْلُهُ
munajat.tr: ilahi tawalla min amri ma anta ahluhu
munajat.en: My God, take charge of my affair in the way that befits You,

munajat.ar: وَعُدْ عَلَيَّ بِفَضْلِكَ عَلَىٰ مُذْنِبٍ قَدْ غَمَرَهُ جَهْلُهُ
munajat.tr: wa `ud `alayya bifadlika `ala mudhnibin qad ghamarahu jahluhu
munajat.en: and return to me with Your bounty, a sinner engulfed by his own ignorance.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي قَدْ سَتَرْتَ عَلَيَّ ذُنُوباً فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا
munajat.tr: ilahi qad satarta `alayya dhunuban fi alddunya
munajat.en: My God, You have veiled many of my sins in this world,

munajat.ar: وَأَنَا أَحْوَجُ إِلَىٰ سَتْرِهَا عَلَيَّ مِنْكَ فِي ٱلأُخْرَىٰ
munajat.tr: wa ana ahwaju ila satriha `alayya minka fi al-ukhra
munajat.en: and I am in greater need of You veiling them for me in the next.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِى قَدْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَىَّ إِذْ لَمْ تُظْهِرْها لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ عِبادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ
munajat.tr: Ilahee qad ahsanta ilayya idh lam tudhhirha li-ahadin min `ibadika alssalihina
munajat.en: My God, You have been good to me in that You did not reveal them to any of Your righteous servants,

munajat.ar: فَلاَ تَفْضَحْنِي يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ عَلَىٰ رُؤُوسِ ٱلْأَشْهَادِ
munajat.tr: fala tafdahni yawma alqiyamati `ala ru'usi al-ashhadi
munajat.en: so do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection in front of all the witnesses.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي جُودُكَ بَسَطَ أَمَلِي
munajat.tr: ilahi juduka basata amali
munajat.en: My God, Your generosity has widened my hope,

munajat.ar: وَعَفْوُكَ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ عَمَلِي
munajat.tr: wa `afwuka afdalu min `amali
munajat.en: and Your pardon is greater than my deeds.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي فَسُرَّنِي بِلِقَائِكَ يَوْمَ تَقْضِي فِيهِ بَيْنَ عِبَادِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi fasurrani biliqa'ika yawma taqdi fihi bayna `ibadika
munajat.en: My God, so gladden me with meeting You on the day You judge between Your servants.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي ٱعْتِذَارِي إِلَيْكَ ٱعْتِذَارُ مَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَغْنِ عَنْ قَبُولِ عُذْرِهِ
munajat.tr: ilahi i`tidhari ilayka i`tidharu man lam yastaghni `an qabuli `udhrihi
munajat.en: My God, my plea of excuse to You is the plea of one who cannot do without its being accepted,

munajat.ar: فَٱقْبَلْ عُذْرِي يَا أَكْرَمَ مَنِ ٱعْتَذَرَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلْمُسِيئُونَ
munajat.tr: faqbal `udhri ya akrama man i`tadhara ilayhi almusi'una
munajat.en: so accept my excuse, O Most Generous of all to whom wrongdoers have ever brought their excuses.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي لاَ تَرُدَّ حَاجَتِي
munajat.tr: ilahi la tarudda hajati
munajat.en: My God, do not turn my need away,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ تُخَيِّبْ طَمَعِي
munajat.tr: wa la tukhayyib tama`i
munajat.en: do not disappoint my yearning,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ تَقْطَعْ مِنْكَ رَجَائِي وَأَمَلِي
munajat.tr: wa la taqta` minka raja'i wa amali
munajat.en: and do not cut off my hope and expectation in You.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي لَوْ أَرَدْتَ هَوَانِي لَمْ تَهْدِنِي
munajat.tr: ilahi law aradta hawani lam tahdini
munajat.en: My God, had You wished to humiliate me, You would not have guided me,

munajat.ar: وَلَوْ أَرَدْتَ فَضِيحَتِي لَمْ تُعَافِنِي
munajat.tr: wa law aradta fadihati lam tu`afini
munajat.en: and had You wished to expose me, You would not have kept me safe.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي مَا أَظُنُّكَ تَرُدُّنِي فِي حَاجَةٍ قَدْ أَفْنَيْتُ عُمْرِي فِي طَلَبِهَا مِنْكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi ma azunnuka tarudduni fi hajatin qad afnaytu `umri fi talabiha minka
munajat.en: My God, I cannot think that You would turn me away in a need I have spent my whole life asking You for.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي فَلَكَ ٱلْحَمْدُ أَبَداً أَبَداً دَائِماً سَرْمَداً
munajat.tr: ilahi falaka alhamdu abadan abadan da'iman sarmadan
munajat.en: My God, to You belongs all praise, for ever and ever, always and without end,

munajat.ar: يَزِيدُ وَلاَ يَبِيدُ كَمَا تُحِبُّ وَتَرْضَىٰ
munajat.tr: yazidu wa la yabidu kama tuhibbu wa tarda
munajat.en: increasing and never fading, as You love and are pleased with.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ أَخَذْتَنِي بِجُرْمِي أَخَذْتُكَ بِعَفْوِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in akhadhtani bijurmi akhadhtuka bi`afwika
munajat.en: My God, if You seize me for my crime, I will hold on to Your pardon;

munajat.ar: وَإِنْ أَخَذْتَنِي بِذُنُوبِي أَخَذْتُكَ بِمَغْفِرَتِكَ
munajat.tr: wa in akhadhtani bidhunubi akhadhtuka bimaghfiratika
munajat.en: if You seize me for my sins, I will hold on to Your forgiveness;

munajat.ar: وَإِنْ أَدْخَلْتَنِي ٱلنَّارَ أَعْلَمْتُ أَهْلَهَا أَنِّي أُحِبُّكَ
munajat.tr: wa in adkhaltani alnnara a`lamtu ahlaha anni uhibbuka
munajat.en: and if You put me into the Fire, I will tell its people that I love You.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ كَانَ صَغُرَ فِي جَنْبِ طَاعَتِكَ عَمَلِي
munajat.tr: ilahi in kana saghura fi janbi ta`atika `amali
munajat.en: My God, if my deeds are small beside what obedience to You deserves,

munajat.ar: فَقَدْ كَبُرَ فِي جَنْبِ رَجَائِكَ أَمَلِي
munajat.tr: faqad kabura fi janbi raja'ika amali
munajat.en: my hope has grown great beside what hope in You allows.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي كَيْفَ أَنْقَلِبُ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ بِٱلْخَيْبَةِ مَحْرُوماً
munajat.tr: ilahi kayfa anqalibu min `indika bilkhaybati mahruman
munajat.en: My God, how could I turn back from You disappointed and deprived,

munajat.ar: وَقَدْ كَانَ حُسْنُ ظَنِّي بِجُودِكَ أَنْ تَقْلِبَنِي بِٱلنَّجَاةِ مَرْحُوماً
munajat.tr: wa qad kana husnu zanni bijudika an taqlibani bilnnajati marhuman
munajat.en: when my good opinion of Your generosity was that You would send me back saved and shown mercy?

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي وَقَدْ أَفْنَيْتُ عُمْرِي فِي شِرَّةِ ٱلسَّهْوِ عَنْكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi wa qad afnaytu `umri fi shirrati alssahwi `anka
munajat.en: My God, I have spent my life in the wildness of heedlessness of You,

munajat.ar: وَأَبْلَيْتُ شَبَابِي فِي سَكْرَةِ ٱلتَّبَاعُدِ مِنْكَ
munajat.tr: wa ablaytu shababi fi sakrati alttaba`udi minka
munajat.en: and worn out my youth in the drunkenness of distance from You.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي فَلَمْ أَسْتَيْقِظْ أَيَّامَ ٱغْتِرَارِي بِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi falam astayqiz ayyama ightirari bika
munajat.en: My God, I did not wake up in the days when I was deluded about You

munajat.ar: وَرُكُونِي إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ سَخَطِكَ
munajat.tr: wa rukuni ila sabili sakhatika
munajat.en: and leaning towards the path that brings Your displeasure.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ وَٱبْنُ عَبْدِكَ قَائِمٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi wa ana `abduka wabnu `abdika qa'imun bayna yadayka
munajat.en: My God, I am Your servant and the son of Your servant, standing before You,

munajat.ar: مُتَوَسِّلٌ بِكَرَمِكَ إِلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: mutawassilun bikaramika ilayka
munajat.en: seeking a way to You through Your own generosity.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي أَنَا عَبْدٌ أَتَنَصَّلُ إِلَيْكَ مِمَّا كُنْتُ أُوَاجِهُكَ بِهِ
munajat.tr: ilahi ana `abdun atanassalu ilayka mimma kuntu uwajihuka bihi
munajat.en: My God, I am a servant who disowns before You what I used to confront You with,

munajat.ar: مِنْ قِلَّةِ ٱسْتِحْيَائِي مِنْ نَظَرِكَ
munajat.tr: min qillati istihya'i min nazarika
munajat.en: my lack of shame before Your gaze,

munajat.ar: وَأَطْلُبُ ٱلْعَفْوَ مِنْكَ إِذ ِٱلْعَفْوُ نَعْتٌ لِكَرَمِكَ
munajat.tr: wa atlubu al`afwa minka idh al`afwu na`tun likaramika
munajat.en: and I ask You for pardon, for pardon is a mark of Your generosity.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي لَمْ يَكُنْ لِي حَوْلٌ فَأَنْتَقِلَ بِهِ عَنْ مَعْصِيَتِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi lam yakun li hawlun fa-antaqila bihi `an ma`siyatika
munajat.en: My God, I had no strength of my own to move away from disobeying You,

munajat.ar: إِلاَّ فِي وَقْتٍ أَيْقَظْتَنِي لِمَحَبَّتِكَ
munajat.tr: illa fi waqtin ayqaztani limahabbatika
munajat.en: except at the moment You woke me up to Your love.

munajat.ar: وَكَمَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ أَكُونَ كُنْتُ
munajat.tr: wa kama aradta an akuna kuntu
munajat.en: And just as You willed me to be, so I became.

munajat.ar: فَشَكَرْتُكَ بِإِدْخَالِي فِي كَرَمِكَ
munajat.tr: fashakartuka bi-idkhali fi karamika
munajat.en: So I thanked You for bringing me into Your generosity,

munajat.ar: وَلِتَطْهِيرِ قَلْبِي مِنْ أَوْسَاخِ ٱلْغَفْلَةِ عَنْكَ
munajat.tr: wa litathiri qalbi min awsakhi alghaflati `anka
munajat.en: and for cleansing my heart of the filth of heedlessness of You.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي ٱنْظُرْ إِلَيَّ نَظَرَ مَنْ نَادَيْتَهُ فَأَجَابَكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi unzur ilayya nazara man nadaytahu fa-ajabaka
munajat.en: My God, look upon me as You look upon one whom You called and he answered You,

munajat.ar: وَٱسْتَعْمَلْتَهُ بِمَعُونَتِكَ فَأَطَاعَكَ
munajat.tr: wasta`maltahu bima`unatika fa-ata`aka
munajat.en: and whom You put to work by Your help and he obeyed You.

munajat.ar: يَا قَرِيباً لاَ يَبْعُدُ عَنِ ٱلْمُغْتَرِّ بِهِ
munajat.tr: ya qariban la yab`udu `an almughtarri bihi
munajat.en: O Near One, who is not far from the one who is deluded about Him,

munajat.ar: وَيَا جَوَاداً لاَ يَبْخَلُ عَمَّنْ رَجَا ثَوَابَهُ
munajat.tr: wa ya jawadan la yabkhalu `amman raja thawabahu
munajat.en: and O Generous One, who is not stingy with the one who hopes for His reward.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي هَبْ لِي قَلْباً يُدْنِيهِ مِنْكَ شَوْقُهُ
munajat.tr: ilahi hab li qalban yudnihi minka shawquhu
munajat.en: My God, grant me a heart whose longing brings it near to You,

munajat.ar: وَلِسَاناً يُرْفَعُ إِلَيْكَ صِدْقُهُ
munajat.tr: wa lisanan yurfa`u ilayka sidquhu
munajat.en: a tongue whose truthfulness is raised up to You,

munajat.ar: وَنَظَراً يُقَرِّبُهُ مِنْكَ حَقُّهُ
munajat.tr: wa nazaran yuqarribuhu minka haqquhu
munajat.en: and a gaze whose truth draws it close to You.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنَّ مَنْ تَعَرَّفَ بِكَ غَيْرُ مَجْهُولٍ
munajat.tr: ilahi inna man ta`arrafa bika ghayru majhulin
munajat.en: My God, whoever is made known through You is never unknown,

munajat.ar: وَمَنْ لاَذَ بِكَ غَيْرُ مَخْذُولٍ
munajat.tr: wa man ladha bika ghayru makhdhulin
munajat.en: whoever takes refuge in You is never abandoned,

munajat.ar: وَمَنْ أَقْبَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ غَيْرُ مَمْلُولٍ
munajat.tr: wa man aqbalta `alayhi ghayru mamlulin
munajat.en: and whoever You turn towards is never grown weary of.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنَّ مَنِ ٱنْتَهَجَ بِكَ لَمُسْتَنِيرٌ
munajat.tr: ilahi inna man intahaja bika lamustanirun
munajat.en: My God, whoever takes his path through You is surely illuminated,

munajat.ar: وَإِنَّ مَنِ ٱعْتَصَمَ بِكَ لَمُسْتَجِيرٌ
munajat.tr: wa inna man i`tasama bika lamustajirun
munajat.en: and whoever holds fast to You has surely found protection.

munajat.ar: وَقَدْ لُذْتُ بِكَ يَا إِلٰهِي فَلاَ تُخَيِّبْ ظَنِّي مِنْ رَحْمَتِكَ
munajat.tr: wa qad ludhtu bika ya ilahi fala tukhayyib zanni min rahmatika
munajat.en: I have taken refuge in You, my God, so do not disappoint my good opinion of Your mercy,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ تَحْجُبْنِي عَنْ رَأْفَتِكَ
munajat.tr: wa la tahjubni `an ra'fatika
munajat.en: and do not veil me from Your tenderness.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي أَقِمْنِي فِي أَهْلِ وِلايَتِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi aqimni fi ahli wilayatika
munajat.en: My God, set me among the people of Your friendship and guardianship (wilayah),

munajat.ar: مُقَامَ مَنْ رَجَا ٱلزِّيَادَةَ مِنْ مَحَبَّتِكَ
munajat.tr: muqama man raja alzziyadata min mahabbatika
munajat.en: in the station of one who hopes for more of Your love.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي وَأَلْهِمْنِي وَلَهاً بِذِكْرِكَ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi wa alhimni walahan bidhikrika ila dhikrika
munajat.en: My God, inspire me with an ardent love of Your remembrance, leading on to more of Your remembrance,

munajat.ar: وَهِمَّتِي فِي رَوْحِ نَجَاحِ أَسْمَائِكَ وَمَحَلِّ قُدْسِكَ
munajat.tr: wa himmati fi rawhi najahi asma'ika wa mahalli qudsika
munajat.en: and set my resolve on the joy of success in Your names and the place of Your holiness.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي بِكَ عَلَيْكَ إِلاَّ أَلْحَقْتَنِي بِمَحَلِّ أَهْلِ طَاعَتِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi bika `alayka illa alhaqtani bimahalli ahli ta`atika
munajat.en: My God, by You, I implore You, join me to the place of the people who obey You,

munajat.ar: وَٱلْمَثْوَىٰ ٱلصَّالِحِ مِنْ مَرْضَاتِكَ
munajat.tr: walmathwa alssalihi min mardatika
munajat.en: and to the righteous dwelling of Your good pleasure.

munajat.ar: فَإِنِّي لاَ أَقْدِرُ لِنَفْسِي دَفْعاً
munajat.tr: fa'inni la aqdiru linafsi daf`an
munajat.en: For I cannot ward off any harm from my soul,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ أَمْلِكُ لَهَا نَفْعاً
munajat.tr: wa la amliku laha naf`an
munajat.en: nor can I bring it any benefit.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي أَنَا عَبْدُكَ ٱلضَّعِيفُ ٱلْمُذْنِبُ
munajat.tr: ilahi ana `abduka aldda`ifu almudhnibu
munajat.en: My God, I am Your weak, sinful servant,

munajat.ar: وَمَمْلُوكُكَ ٱلْمُنِيبُ
munajat.tr: wa mamlukuka almunibu
munajat.en: and Your bondsman who turns back to You.

munajat.ar: فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي مِمَّنْ صَرَفْتَ عَنْهُ وَجْهَكَ
munajat.tr: fala taj`alni mimman sarafta `anhu wajhaka
munajat.en: So do not place me among those from whom You have turned Your face away,

munajat.ar: وَحَجَبَهُ سَهْوُهُ عَنْ عَفْوِكَ
munajat.tr: wa hajabahu sahwuhu `an `afwika
munajat.en: and whose heedlessness has veiled them from Your pardon.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي هَبْ لي كَمَالَ ٱلاِنْقِطَاعِ إِلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi hab li kamala alinqita`i ilayka
munajat.en: My God, grant me complete detachment from all else, devoted wholly to You,

munajat.ar: وَأَنِرْ أَبْصَارَ قُلُوبِنَا بِضِيَاءِ نَظَرِهَا إِلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: wa anir absara qulubina bidiya'i nazariha ilayka
munajat.en: and illuminate the eyes of our hearts with the light of their gazing at You,

munajat.ar: حَتَّىٰ تَخْرِقَ أَبْصَارُ ٱلْقُلُوبِ حُجُبَ ٱلنُّورِ
munajat.tr: hatta takhriqa absaru alqulubi hujuba alnnuri
munajat.en: until the eyes of the hearts pierce the veils of light

munajat.ar: فَتَصِلَ إِلَىٰ مَعْدِنِ ٱلْعَظَمَةِ
munajat.tr: fatasila ila ma`dini al`azamati
munajat.en: and reach the very source of Majesty,

munajat.ar: وَتَصِيرَ أَرْوَاحُنَا مُعَلَّقَةً بِعِزِّ قُدْسِكَ
munajat.tr: wa tasira arwahuna mu`allaqatan bi`izzi qudsika
munajat.en: and our souls become suspended from the glory of Your holiness.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي وَٱجْعَلْنِي مِمَّنْ نَادَيْتَهُ فَأَجَابَكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi waj`alni mimman nadaytahu fa-ajabaka
munajat.en: My God, place me among those whom You called and they answered You,

munajat.ar: وَلاحَظْتَهُ فَصَعِقَ لِجَلالِكَ
munajat.tr: wa lahaztahu fasa`iqa lijalalika
munajat.en: and upon whom You glanced so that they swooned before Your Majesty,

munajat.ar: فَنَاجَيْتَهُ سِرّاً وَعَمِلَ لَكَ جَهْراً
munajat.tr: fanajaytahu sirran wa `amila laka jahran
munajat.en: so You spoke with them in secret, and they worked for You in the open.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي لَمْ أُسَلِّطْ عَلَىٰ حُسْنِ ظَنِّي قُنُوطَ ٱلأَيَاسِ
munajat.tr: ilahi lam usallit `ala husni zanni qunuta al-ayasi
munajat.en: My God, I have not let the gloom of despair overpower my good opinion of You,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ ٱنْقَطَعَ رَجَائِي مِنْ جَمِيلِ كَرَمِكَ
munajat.tr: wa la inqata`a raja'i min jamili karamika
munajat.en: nor has my hope in Your beautiful generosity been cut off.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ كَانَتِ ٱلْخَطَايَا قَدْ أَسْقَطَتْنِي لَدَيْكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in kanat alkhataya qad asqatatni ladayka
munajat.en: My God, if my mistakes have made me fall low in Your sight,

munajat.ar: فَٱصْفَحْ عَنِّي بِحُسْنِ تَوَكُّلِي عَلَيْكَ
munajat.tr: fasfah `anni bihusni tawakkuli `alayka
munajat.en: then overlook them for me, for the sake of my good trust in You.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ حَطَّتْنِيَ ٱلذُّنُوبُ مِنْ مَكَارِمِ لُطْفِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in hattatni aldhdhunubu min makarimi lutfika
munajat.en: My God, if my sins have brought me down from the honours of Your kindness,

munajat.ar: فَقَدْ نَبَّهَنِي ٱلْيَقِينُ إِلَىٰ كَرَمِ عَطْفِكَ
munajat.tr: faqad nabbahani alyaqinu ila karami `atfika
munajat.en: certainty has awakened me to the generosity of Your compassion.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ أَنَامَتْنِيَ ٱلْغَفْلَةُ عَنِ ٱلإِسْتِعْدَادِ لِلِقَائِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in anamatni alghaflatu `an alisti`dadi liliqa'ika
munajat.en: My God, if heedlessness has lulled me to sleep from preparing to meet You,

munajat.ar: فَقَدْ نَبَّهَتْنِي ٱلْمَعْرِفَةُ بِكَرَمِ آلاَئِكَ
munajat.tr: faqad nabbahatni alma`rifatu bikarami ala'ika
munajat.en: knowledge of Your generous blessings has woken me.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي إِنْ دَعَانِي إِلَىٰ ٱلنَّارِ عَظِيمُ عِقَابِكَ
munajat.tr: ilahi in da`ani ila alnnari `azimu `iqabika
munajat.en: My God, if the greatness of Your punishment has called me towards the Fire,

munajat.ar: فَقَدْ دَعَانِي إِلَىٰ ٱلْجَنَّةِ جَزِيلُ ثَوَابِكَ
munajat.tr: faqad da`ani ila aljannati jazilu thawabika
munajat.en: the abundance of Your reward has called me towards the Garden.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي فَلَكَ أَسْأَلُ وَإِلَيْكَ أَبْتَهِلُ وَأَرْغَبُ
munajat.tr: ilahi falaka as'alu wa ilayka abtahilu wa arghabu
munajat.en: My God, so it is You I ask, and to You I humbly plead and turn in longing,

munajat.ar: وَأَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
munajat.tr: wa as'aluka an tusalliya `ala muhammadin wa ali muhammadin
munajat.en: and I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad,

munajat.ar: وَأَنْ تَجْعَلَنِي مِمَّنْ يُدِيمُ ذِكْرَكَ
munajat.tr: wa an taj`alani mimman yudimu dhikraka
munajat.en: and to make me among those who remember You constantly,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ يَنْقُضُ عَهْدَكَ
munajat.tr: wa la yanqudu `ahdaka
munajat.en: who do not break their covenant with You,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ يَغْفُلُ عَنْ شُكْرِكَ
munajat.tr: wa la yaghfulu `an shukrika
munajat.en: who are never heedless of thanking You,

munajat.ar: وَلاَ يَسْتَخِفُّ بِأَمْرِكَ
munajat.tr: wa la yastakhiffu bi-amrika
munajat.en: and who never take Your command lightly.

munajat.ar: إِلٰهِي وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِنُورِ عِزِّكَ ٱلأَبْهَجِ
munajat.tr: ilahi wa alhiqni binuri `izzika al-abhaji
munajat.en: My God, join me to the light of Your most radiant glory,

munajat.ar: فَأَكُونَ لَكَ عَارِفاً
munajat.tr: fa-akuna laka `arifan
munajat.en: so that I may truly know You,

munajat.ar: وَعَنْ سِوَاكَ مُنْحَرِفاً
munajat.tr: wa `an siwaka munharifan
munajat.en: turn away from everything besides You,

munajat.ar: وَمِنْكَ خَائِفاً مُرَاقِباً
munajat.tr: wa minka kha'ifan muraqiban
munajat.en: and stand in awe of You, ever watchful of You,

munajat.ar: يَا ذَا ٱلْجَلاَلِ وَٱلإِكْرَامِ
munajat.tr: ya dha aljalali wal-ikrami
munajat.en: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour.

munajat.ar: وَصَلَّىٰ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولِهِ وَآلِهِ ٱلطَّاهِرِينَ
munajat.tr: wa salla allahu `ala muhammadin rasulihi wa alihi alttahirina
munajat.en: And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, His Messenger, and upon his pure family,

munajat.ar: وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيماً كَثِيراً
munajat.tr: wa sallama tasliman kathiran
munajat.en: and grant them abundant peace.

# Preface, Acknowledgments, Introduction
## Source
book.txt (camp Drive PDF), pages xi to xix. Page refs are printed book pages.
## Summary
- Preface (p.xi-xii): the four archetypes were first presented as lectures at the C. G. Jung Institute of Chicago and as audiotapes. They map Jung's "double quaternio": the archetypal Self in four quarters, with two built-in oppositions: King (or Queen)/Magician and Lover/Warrior. The book is an "operator's manual for the male psyche" and the first of a planned five-volume series.
- Dedication to poet Robert Bly. Epigraph: William Blake, The Four Zoas, "Four Mighty Ones are in every Man".
- Introduction (p.xv-xix): answers the question from Bill Moyers's interview with Bly, "Where are the initiated men of power today?" Causes of the crisis in masculinity: (1) the disappearing father, (2) the loss of ritual initiation (blamed partly on the Reformation and Enlightenment; Victor Turner's "mere ceremonial"), (3) patriarchy, which the authors define as the expression of the immature masculine (Boy psychology), based on fear of women and of real men.
- Boy psychology shows as abuse/violence, passivity/weakness, or oscillation between the two.
- Men in therapy lacked connection to deep masculine energies, not to the inner feminine. Through meditation, prayer and active imagination they became "strong, centered, and generative".
- Core claim: we need more masculine power, but mature masculine power; "a sense of calmness about masculine power".
## Key quotes
- "Where are the initiated men of power today?" (p.xv)
- "Patriarchy is the expression of the immature masculine. It is the expression of Boy psychology" (p.xvii)
- "We need more. But we need more of the mature masculine." (p.xviii)
- "We need to learn to love and be loved by the mature masculine." (p.xix)
## Concepts
initiation, Boy psychology, Man psychology, patriarchy as immaturity, double quaternio
## Practices
meditation, prayer, active imagination (p.xviii)
## Camp link (interpretation)
SW Camp is a modern initiation: sacred space plus elders (sheikhs, coaches) plus ordeal (training) plus prayer.

# Chapter 1: The Crisis in Masculine Ritual Process (p.3-7)
## Summary
- A man who "can't get himself together" is fragmented: he probably never had ritual initiation, so he remains a boy "because no one has shown him the way" (p.3).
- Cro-Magnon caves were likely initiation sanctuaries "by men for men" (p.3-4). Eliade and Turner show initiation survives in tribal cultures.
- Movies work like myths; The Emerald Forest shows initiation: the chief says "Tomme, your time has come to die", ordeal by ants, bath, "The boy is dead and the man is born!", vision of his animal soul (eagle), then marriage, brave, chief (p.4-5).
- Life's fundamental dynamic: moving from diffuse to more structured identity (p.5).
- Pseudo-initiations: military boot camp (possible exception), city gangs, prisons. They produce skewed, abusive "manhood" (p.5).
- Boy psychology is sadomasochistic, seeking dominance; Man psychology is "nurturing and generative" (p.6).
- Initiation requires a death of the boy Ego, which is resurrected "with a new, subordinate relationship to a previously unknown power or center" (p.6).
- Two containers of real ritual: sacred space (Eliade) sealed from the outside world, and a trustworthy ritual elder (p.6-7). Initiates "learn to submit to the pain of life" (p.6).
- Scarcity of mature men means scarce elders; men feel anxious, impotent, ashamed, and seek "the generative, affirming, and empowering father" (p.7).
## Key quotes
- "In psychological terms, the boy Ego must 'die.'" (p.6)
- "Submission to the power of the mature masculine energies always brings forth a new masculine personality that is marked by calm, compassion, clarity of vision, and generativity." (p.6)
- "real men are not wantonly violent or hostile" (p.5)
## Concepts
ritual initiation, pseudo-initiation, sacred space, ritual elder, Ego death
## Camp link (interpretation)
The camp structure (secluded venue, sheikhs and coaches, ordeal, submission to God as the "new center") maps closely to the authors' two containers. Ask: what in me needs to "die" this week?

# Chapter 2: Masculine Potentials (p.9-11)
## Summary
- Jungian hope: deep within every man are "blueprints" or "hard wiring" for the calm, mature masculine: archetypes or "primordial images" in the collective unconscious (p.9).
- Imprinting analogy: ducklings are wired for "mother"; the outer parent may fail, but the archetype remains (p.9-10).
- Archetypes skewed by inadequate or hostile parents become crippling problems; Winnicott's "good enough" parents let us access them positively (p.10).
- Evidence: dreams, behaviour patterns, world mythology (dying-resurrecting God) (p.10).
- Every man has an Anima (feminine subpersonality); every woman an Animus (p.11).
- Aim: help men access positive archetypal potentials for themselves and others (p.11).
## Key quotes
- "deep within every man are blueprints, what we can also call 'hard wiring,' for the calm and positive mature masculine." (p.9)
## Concepts
archetype, collective unconscious, imprinting, good enough parenting, Anima/Animus
## Camp link (interpretation)
As a new father (newborn, Hassan), Moe is now the "outer" figure his children's archetypes imprint on.

# Chapter 3: Boy Psychology (p.13-42)
## Summary
- Opening list: drug dealer, wife beater, crabby boss, "yes man", "holier than thou" minister, absent father, coach who ridicules: "They are all boys pretending to be men" (p.13). Controlling, hostile behaviour is mistaken for strength but shows "the vulnerability of the wounded boy" (p.13).
- Healthy boyishness = playfulness, fun, open-minded adventure (p.14).
- Structure: each archetype is a triangle: fullness at the top, a bipolar shadow (active and passive poles) at the base. Shadow = lack of cohesion; maturity integrates the poles (p.14). Under stress the Ego flips between poles (p.25-26).
- Order of onset: Divine Child, then Precocious and Oedipal Child, then Hero (p.14).
- "the boy is father to the man": Divine Child to King, Precocious Child to Magician, Oedipal Child to Lover, Hero to Warrior (p.15). Mature Self = "a pyramid over a pyramid"; boy energies are built on, not demolished (p.15, Fig 1-3 p.16-20).
## Divine Child (p.15-27)
- Fullness: Christ child, Moses, Zoroaster, Sargon, Buddha, Krishna; centre of the universe yet helpless; threatened by "Herods" (p.15-20). In therapy, dreams of a radiant baby boy and the urge to have children signal new life (p.20). New life must be protected: get the Divine Child "to Egypt" (p.21).
- Orpheus bringing all animals into harmony prefigures the King (p.21). Story of the boy singing under the oak tree until it filled with birds (p.21-22).
- Freud (Id), Adler (power drive), Kohut (grandiose self) see its shadow; Jungians see the source of life. Both are right (p.22-23).
- Shadow active: High Chair Tyrant: banging spoon, rejects food and love; arrogance (hubris), childishness, irresponsibility; later the self-sabotaging CEO, the boss who wants yes men, Icarus; turned inward it is the perfectionist who drives himself to ulcers and heart attacks (p.23-25). "hubris is always followed by nemesis" (p.24). He wants "to be", not "to do" (p.25).
- Shadow passive: Weakling Prince: no enthusiasm or initiative, coddled, hypochondriacal, rules by whining helplessness, but stabs siblings with sarcasm (p.25).
- Accessing: "acknowledge him, but not identify with him" (p.26). Leaders need the creative playful Child. Against "the curse of normalcy" (p.26). Roman "genius" as guardian spirit (p.26-27).
- Two questions: how am I manifesting the Tyrant and the Weakling? How am I honouring or blocking my creative Child? (p.27)
## Precocious Child (p.27-33)
- Fullness: boy Imhotep reading; curiosity, the "why", eager learning, sharing, talents, reflective yet reaching out to help; moves toward the Magician (p.27-28).
- Shadow active: Know-It-All Trickster: creates appearances, betrays, intimidates, dominates conversations, smug (p.28-29). Positive side: deflates inflation, like the court Fool, and like the "troublemaker for truth" figure in Job (p.30). Inner Trickster: printer fails before your "brilliant" presentation, keys locked in the car: "Hubris leads to nemesis" (p.31). Jacob tricking Esau (p.32). Passive-aggressive; authority problem; fuelled by envy; "Envy blocks creativity" (p.32). Activated by parental depreciation; "has no heroes" (p.33).
- Shadow passive: Dummy: seems dull, slow, inept, naive, but often masks hidden grandiosity; secretly also a Trickster (p.33).
## Oedipal Child (p.33-37)
- All immature energies are overly tied to Mother (p.33). Fullness: passion, wonder, warmth, connectedness, origins of spirituality, a yearning for the infinitely good Great Mother beyond the real mother (p.34). "God. All-Mother. Mighty!" slip story (p.34-35).
- Shadow active: Mama's Boy: tied to apron strings; Oedipus and Adonis inflated; Don Juan chasing the Goddess from woman to woman; compulsive masturbation and pornography; "does not want to take responsibility" (p.35-36).
- Shadow passive: Dreamer: isolated, relationships with intangible things, withdrawn, depressed; masks pique at not possessing Mother (p.36-37).
## Hero (p.37-42)
- The Hero is "the most advanced form" of Boy psychology but immature if it governs adulthood (p.37).
- Shadow active: Grandstander Bully: must impress and dominate, rage when challenged, not a team player; Vietnam officers, Top Gun's Maverick vs Iceman ("The difference between the Hero and the mature Warrior"), Patton (p.37-39). "You boys are good. But you're not as good as you think you are." (p.38). Denial of death, failure to know limits (p.39).
- Shadow passive: Coward: avoids physical, emotional and intellectual confrontation, a doormat, then erupts into the hidden Bully (p.39-40).
- Purpose: helps the boy break from Mother, test limits, "establish a beachhead" against the unconscious (p.40). "We need a great rebirth of the heroic in our world." (p.41)
- The "death" of the Hero = meeting his limitations and dark side: "the enemy is himself" (p.41). "True humility ... consists of two things. The first is knowing our limitations. And the second is getting the help we need." (p.41)
## Key quotes
- "They are all boys pretending to be men." (p.13)
- "the boy is father to the man." (p.15)
- "we need to acknowledge him, but not identify with him." (p.26)
- "Envy blocks creativity." (p.32)
- "He has met the enemy, and the enemy is himself." (p.41)
- "True humility ... knowing our limitations ... getting the help we need." (p.41)
## Shadow poles (grep: SHADOW)
- SHADOW Divine Child: High Chair Tyrant (active) / Weakling Prince (passive)
- SHADOW Precocious Child: Know-It-All Trickster (active) / Dummy (passive)
- SHADOW Oedipal Child: Mama's Boy (active) / Dreamer (passive)
- SHADOW Hero: Grandstander Bully (active) / Coward (passive)
## Practices
- Ask the two Divine Child questions (p.27).
- Protect new growth from inner "Herods" (p.21).
- Study the Trickster to break its compulsion (graduate student example, p.32).
- Humility: know limits, get help (p.41).
## Camp link (interpretation)
Training and wrestling at camp will expose Hero shadows quickly (grandstanding or caving). The camp's "look after your brother" is the team-player antidote to the Bully.

# Chapter 4: Man Psychology (p.43-45)
## Summary
- Infantile "gravitational" pull resists maturity; build the pyramid of manhood on top of the pyramids of boyhood, like the Maya who built over old structures without demolishing them (p.43).
- Goal image: standing on top as "Lord of the Four Quarters" (p.43).
- Techniques: dream analysis, re-entering dreams, active imagination, psychotherapy, meditation on positive aspects of archetypes, prayer, ritual with a spiritual elder, spiritual discipline (p.43).
- The four mature forms are King, Warrior, Magician, Lover; they overlap. "A good King is always also a Warrior, a Magician, and a Lover." (p.44)
- Boy energies: Divine Child gives rise to Oedipal Child; Precocious Child helps the Ego differentiate; all give rise to the Hero, which breaks the boy free of the "feminine" unconscious (p.44).
- Archetypes are like a magnet under paper with iron filings: seen only by effects (p.44).
- Board meeting model (from Jean Shinoda Bolen): Ego is the chair, archetypes are board members; hear each, then the chair decides (p.44-45).
- "we have to take responsibility for what we're not responsible for" (p.45). Ours is a psychological, individual age; what institutions did, we must now do consciously ourselves (p.45).
## Key quotes
- "A good King is always also a Warrior, a Magician, and a Lover." (p.44)
- "we have to take responsibility for what we're not responsible for." (p.45)
## Practices
- Board meeting exercise: list a decision, let each archetype speak, then decide as chair (p.44-45).
- Prayer, meditation, active imagination, spiritual discipline (p.43).
## Camp link (interpretation)
The camp's list of means (prayer, discipline, elders) is close to the authors' toolkit on p.43.

# Chapter 5: The King (p.49-73)
## Summary
- The King is primal, first in importance, includes the other three, yet usually "comes on line last" (p.49). The Divine Child "seasoned and complex, wise" and selfless; "the wisdom of Solomon"; the imago Dei, Anthropos, Atman (p.49).
- Kingship, not the mortal king, is sacred: "The king is dead; long live the king!" The mortal man is a vehicle in service of the realm (p.49-50). Frazer: failing kings were ritually killed (p.50).
- Dream of the Chinese emperor: a soldier of fortune flees into a cave, finds the emperor in a green garden, kneels; the emperor with "fatherly compassion" says "You have to die"; he submits with peace. The Hero meets his limits and is reconciled with the Father (p.50-51).
- John Weir Perry: images of the sacred King arise in psychotic patients and heal; the King is "the central archetype" (p.51-52).
- Two functions of the King in his fullness (p.52):
  1. ORDERING: the king on the Primeval Hill at the Center; world = what he orders; outside is chaos. Ptah's Word, Yahweh; Sargon "He Who Rules the Four Quarters"; Black Elk's hoop; mandalas (Jung) as healing images (p.52-54). Hammurabi receiving laws from Shamash; Moses and the Torah on Sinai (p.54-56). Ma'at, Wisdom, Logos, Dharma, Tao. "The mortal king's first responsibility is to live according to Ma'at" (p.56). Illegitimate kings bring blight (Nefer-rohu prophecy) (p.56-57); Mandate of Heaven (p.57). He lives the order first, enforces it second; defends borders as Warrior (p.57-58). Weak or absent fathers bring chaos to families (p.58).
  2. FERTILITY AND BLESSING: the king wedded to the land; as the king goes, so goes the realm (p.58-60). Blessing = seeing and affirming others; Akhenaton throwing gold rings to loyal men (p.61). "Young men today are starving for blessing from older men" (p.61); being seen "heals and makes whole" (p.61).
- Qualities (p.61-63): order, integration and integrity, stabilises chaotic emotion, calm, centredness, vitality and joy; "a firm but kindly eye"; not envious; rewards creativity; aggressive when order is threatened (Warrior), discerning (Magician), delighting (Lover). Examples: providing for wife and children, supporting your wife's study, attending your son's recital, keeping cool in a meeting, "the clear decision, after careful deliberation"; steward of nature; "minimizes punishment and maximizes praise" (p.62-63).
## Shadow King (p.63-70)
- SHADOW King active: Tyrant. Herod killing the infants: "Whenever the new is born, the Herod within us ... will attack" (p.63). Saul vs David; Caligula declaring himself a god (p.64). Hates beauty, innocence, strength, talent; the father who attacks or ignores his children's joy and achievements (p.64-66). Sexual abuse case; David and Bathsheba, rebuked by Nathan, who repented (p.66). Narcissistic personality: seeks mirroring instead of mirroring others (p.67). Self-serving executives, interviewer who talks only about himself (p.67). Sensitive to criticism; rage over worthlessness (p.67).
- SHADOW King passive: Weakling. Hunger for "Adore me!"; Patton slapping the shell-shocked soldier, projecting his own Weakling (p.68). Paranoia: Herod, Saul, Caligula pacing at night (p.68). The minister undone by a paranoid dissident group (p.68-69).
- Origins: over-adoration (never let down from the high chair, "thinks he is Caesar") or abuse that splits grandiosity into the unconscious, which explodes when promoted: "a Little Hitler" (p.69-70).
## Accessing the King (p.70-73)
- First task: disidentify the Ego from the King; "cognitive distance" (p.70).
- Planet and star image: the Ego orbits the King; the Ego is "servant of a transpersonal Will or Cause", "a steward" (p.70).
- Identification = "usurpation syndrome" (Tyrant, no transpersonal commitment, like Satan's rebellion) (p.71). Extreme disidentification = "abdication syndrome" (Weakling, dependent personality, projecting the King onto a boss, spouse or Fuhrer) (p.71-72). Battle of Otumba: Aztec army fled when its commander fell (p.72).
- Rightly accessed: anxiety drops, centred and calm, speak from inner authority, mirror and bless self and others, transpersonal devotion, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God ... And thy neighbor as thyself" (p.73).
## Key quotes
- "The good and generative King is also a good Warrior, a positive Magician, and a great Lover." (p.49)
- "The mortal king's first responsibility is to live according to Ma'at" (p.56)
- "Young men today are starving for blessing from older men" (p.61)
- "That is the effect of blessing; it heals and makes whole." (p.61)
- "This is the energy that minimizes punishment and maximizes praise." (p.63)
- "Whenever the new is born, the Herod within us (and in our outer lives) will attack." (p.63)
- "the Ego of the mature man needs to think of itself ... as the servant of a transpersonal Will or Cause." (p.70)
## Practices
- Disidentify: "I am a steward, not the King" (p.70).
- Bless: notice and praise people concretely (p.61).
- Live the order personally before enforcing it (p.57).
- Watch for usurpation (inflation) and abdication (handing your centre to others) (p.71-72).
## Camp link (interpretation)
- Faith: the authors' "transpersonal Will or Cause" and the closing commandment line up with tawhid and submission to Allah; the Chinese emperor dream echoes the camp's "know yourself, know your Lord".
- Family: the examples on p.62 (providing, attending, calm) are directly Moe's season with a newborn.
- Film: Vortigern = Tyrant (usurper); Arthur refusing the throne = abdication/Weakling (see film/).

# Chapter 6: The Warrior (p.75-95)
## Summary
- Modern discomfort with Warrior energy (the "soft masculine"); but a repressed archetype "goes underground" and resurfaces as violence (p.75). Goodall's chimpanzees, Ardrey, paintball, war films: the Warrior is instinctual (p.75-76).
- History: Egyptians unify King plus Warrior to expel the Hyksos and spread their civilisation; kshatriya, Zoroastrian kings, David, Marcus Aurelius, Spartans at Thermopylae, Native American "Today is a good day to die!", samurai (p.77-79).
## Warrior in his fullness (p.79-88)
- A total way of life, a "do" (p.79).
- AGGRESSIVENESS: a stance that rouses and takes the offensive; samurai "leap" into battle with full ki; face life frontally, move forward; Patton's speech (p.79-80).
- CLARITY OF THINKING / discernment: always alert, "mindful", a hunter; strategist and tactician; guerrilla warfare; knows his limits, unlike the Hero (p.80). David outmanoeuvring Saul; fencing sharpened a student's thinking (p.80-82).
- AWARENESS OF DEATH: "The Warrior knows the shortness of life"; samurai lived "as if they were already dead"; death as "our eternal companion" (Castaneda's Don Juan); leads to decisive action, never withdrawing (p.82).
- TRAINING AND SKILL: actions become trained reflex through "enormous self-discipline" (p.83). Never overdone, never spends more energy than needed, doesn't talk too much (Yul Brynner, The Magnificent Seven) (p.83).
- POSITIVE MENTAL ATTITUDE AND DISCIPLINE: unconquerable spirit, courage, responsibility, capacity to withstand psychological and physical pain; "No pain, no gain" (p.83-84).
- TRANSPERSONAL COMMITMENT: loyalty to a cause, God, people or task bigger than himself; Lancelot devoted to chivalry, lost when personal romance overrode it (p.84). Relativises personal relationships and "eliminates a great deal of human pettiness" (p.84).
- Samurai story: tracking his lord's assassin, he is spat on, then sheathes his sword and walks away, because killing then would come from personal anger, not duty (p.84-85).
- ASCETIC: hones himself "to bear the unbearable"; Jesus and the Buddha resisting temptation as "spiritual warriors" (p.85). The authors write that "The religion of Islam as a whole is built on Warrior energy" and describe the Prophet as a warrior and jihad "against the powers of evil as they define them" (p.85). (Authors' framing, quoted as written.)
- EMOTIONAL DISTANCE while in the Warrior: "unavailable", "inaccessible", touching the world "sparingly" (p.85-86).
- Samurai exercise: say "There is someone who is afraid ... Now, what can he do about this?" (p.86).
- Destroys only what needs destroying (corruption, tyranny, bad systems) to make way for the new (p.86).
- Combined: with King = steward of the realm (Gorbachev example); with Magician = mastery of self and weapons; with Lover = compassion (GIs carrying wounded children; Full Metal Jacket mercy shot); poet-warriors Marcus Aurelius, Churchill, Mishima, Patton (p.86-87).
- Alone, the Warrior damages relationships: women "for fun", neglected military wives (The Right Stuff), workaholic professionals' families and affairs (p.87-88).
## Shadow Warrior (p.88-94)
- SHADOW Warrior active: Sadist. The Great Santini running his family like the Marines (p.88-89). Detachment "leaves the door open to the 'demon' of cruelty"; feelings must be "not repressed, but under control" (p.89). Cruelty without passion (SS puppies, Darth Vader) and with passion (bloodlust; Apocalypse Now, Platoon, My Lai; Patton "God, I do love it so!") (p.89-90). Hatred of the weak; sadistic drill sergeants (p.90). Rooted in the Hero's fear of the feminine (p.90-92). Compulsive personality: workaholics driven by anxiety, burnout; "If you have to admit to yourself that you really don't take care of yourself ... very probably the Shadow Warrior has got you" (p.92-93). Revolutionaries become new tyrants (p.93). Car salesman's collapse (p.93).
- SHADOW Warrior passive: Masochist. "pushover", "whipped puppy"; can't defend himself, allows others to push him past his limits; doesn't know when to quit a relationship or job; takes abuse then explodes (p.94). "The man who becomes obsessed with 'succeeding' has already failed." (p.94)
## Accessing the Warrior (p.94-95)
- Passive pole signs: dream but don't act, depressed, can't endure pain, stare at the task, walk away from the boss's door (p.95).
- Rightly accessed: "energetic, decisive, courageous, enduring, persevering, and loyal to some greater good"; leavened by King, Magician, Lover: detached yet "warm, compassionate, appreciative, and generative"; fight good fights "for the creation of the new, the just, and the free" (p.95).
## Key quotes
- "there is only one position in which to face the battle of life: frontally" (p.79, samurai tradition)
- "The Warrior knows the shortness of life and how fragile it is." (p.82)
- "There is someone who is afraid ... Now, what can he do about this?" (p.86)
- "Feelings ... not repressed, but under control" (p.89, paraphrase of "not repressed, but under control")
- "The man who becomes obsessed with 'succeeding' has already failed." (p.94)
- "Our war making will be for the creation of the new, the just, and the free." (p.95)
## Practices
- Samurai third-person reframe of fear (p.86).
- Death awareness to cut hesitation (p.82).
- Training until skill becomes reflex; disciplined economy of energy and words (p.83).
- Check the transpersonal cause behind an action; walk away if it is ego (samurai story, p.84-85).
- Self-care check against the compulsive Sadist (p.92-93).
## Camp link (interpretation)
- Discipline and training: daily sessions, punctuality ("Be on time") and Salat al-Layl are Warrior practices.
- Faith: transpersonal commitment = serving Allah; the samurai story parallels the well-known narration of Imam Ali withdrawing from a combatant who spat on him (traditional account, not from the book; verify with sheikhs).
- Combat sports at camp: watch for Sadist (bloodlust) and Masochist (training through injury); the guide says tell a coach if injured.
- Family: Warrior-alone pattern (work over family) is a risk to watch with a newborn at home.

# Chapter 7: The Magician (p.97-118)
## Summary
- Opening: The Right Stuff, Aboriginal elder who "flies too" helping John Glenn by sympathetic magic (p.97). Shamans, scientists, doctors, lawyers, technicians all access the Magician (p.98). Merlin's Camelot; Obi-Wan Kenobi (p.98).
- Twofold: the KNOWER and the MASTER OF TECHNOLOGY; also the "ritual elder" who guides transformation; an initiate who initiates others (p.98). All knowledge needing special training is the Magician's province; apprentices undergo an ordeal (p.98).
- History: the chief once held all four; the shaman knows stars, seasons, herbs, the psyche; confessor, priest, seer; master of containing and channelling power (p.99). Magicians of Mesopotamia and Egypt invented writing, maths, law; Imhotep (p.99-100).
- The Magician is the "bullshit detector": sees through denial, deflates kings' arrogance; court psychotherapist. Nathan's parable of the poor man's lamb to David: "You are the man." David repented (p.100). Merlin initiating Arthur into right use of King energy (The Once and Future King) (p.100-101).
- Gnosticism, alchemy as spiritual transformation, theoretical vs applied science (p.101). Ours is an age of the material Magician but short of spiritual initiation; "chaos is always the result of inadequate accessing of the Magician" (p.102). Subatomic physics and depth psychology (p.102-103). Jung: "I don't believe in God; I know." (p.103)
- Dosing: analysts reveal hidden knowledge in measured doses or it can "blow the Ego structure to bits" (p.104).
- SACRED SPACE is the container: "the step-down transformer", reactor shield, sanctuary, hymns and standard prayers that invoke and shield (p.104). The soldier killed touching the Ark (p.104-105); Raiders of the Lost Ark; Sorcerer's Apprentice; Chernobyl; uncontained encounter groups and rock concerts (p.105-106).
## Magician in his fullness (p.106-110)
- Archetype of awareness and insight; governs the "observing Ego" (p.106). Ego-Self axis: servant of the Self and channeller of its power (p.107).
- Detached observer, like the dam operator watching the gauges (p.107). Regulates the flow of the other archetypes (p.107). In the Warrior as clarity of thinking (p.107).
- Cannot act alone (that is the Warrior), but thinks: careful deliberation on hard decisions (promotion, a son's motivation, budgets) (p.108).
- "the archetype of thoughtfulness and reflection ... the energy of introversion": the capacity to detach from storms and connect with deep inner truth (p.108).
- Crisis example: the driver on ice who went into slow-motion calm and steered safely (p.108-110).
- Entering inner sacred space deliberately: music, a hobby, long walks, meditation (p.110).
- Shaman as fullest human vessel; aim is "fullness of being for all things, through the compassionate application of knowledge and technology" (p.110).
## Shadow Magician (p.111-116)
- SHADOW Magician active: Detached Manipulator ("power Shadow"). Environmental destruction, death-camp technology and the bomb, propaganda (p.111). Directs people in ways they cannot see; withholds information; detached and cruel (p.111). Professors crushing students, doctors withholding diagnoses, legal jargon, therapists hoarding insight, advertisers (p.111-114). Hurts himself too: "the man who thinks too much", lost in pros and cons, a voyeur and armchair adventurer who never lives (p.114). Twilight Zone reader with broken glasses (p.114). Using knowledge "as a weapon to belittle and control" is "black magic" (p.114-115).
- SHADOW Magician passive: Denying "Innocent" One. Wants the status without the responsibility; won't teach, share or know himself; derails others while protesting innocence; hides truth to keep status; driven by envy; slippery, makes you doubt your own intuition (p.115-116).
## Accessing the Magician (p.116-118)
- Out of touch: no inner structure or calm, can't trust thinking, inner chaos, pushed and pulled, passive-aggressive (p.116).
- EXERCISE "focusing" (Eugene Gendlin): sit in an "observation chair", imagine placing each strong feeling on a stack in the middle of the room, observe its colour and shape without judging ("Oh, there you are again!"), then banish it; the contained feeling loses power and can be transformed (p.116-117).
- EXERCISE drawing: the young man with tornado dreams (childhood rage, alcoholic parents, abuse) drew the tornadoes, then drew them in a lead-shielded container, then power lines feeding houses and factories; his life changed, he moved into children's theatre (p.117-118).
- Rightly accessed: clear-sightedness, reflection, technical skill; mixed with King generosity, Warrior courage and Lover connectedness, "for human benefit" (p.118).
## Key quotes
- "The Magician archetype in a man is his 'bullshit detector'" (p.100)
- "You are the man." (Nathan to David, p.100)
- "chaos is always the result of inadequate accessing of the Magician in some vital area of life." (p.102)
- "Sacred space is the container of raw power" (p.104)
- "In his fear of making the wrong decision, he makes none." (p.114)
## Practices
- Focusing / observation chair (p.116-117).
- Contain-and-channel drawing (p.117-118).
- Create inner sacred space: walks, music, meditation (p.110).
- Measured, honest sharing of knowledge; initiate others step by step (p.111, 115).
## Camp link (interpretation)
- The sheikhs and coaches play the ritual-elder Magician role; the camp's private venue and phone-light week are "sacred space" as the authors define it (p.104).
- Prayer and dua as container: the authors themselves list "the hymns and the standard prayers" as containers (p.104). Munajat Sha'baniyya and Salat al-Layl fit here.
- Notebook habit at camp = observing Ego practice.

# Chapter 8: The Lover (p.119-141)
## Summary
- Opening: Shiva's lingam at the Elephanta Caves; phallic symbols as the life-force, "incarnating spirit into flesh" (p.119-120).
- Forms of love: agape ("brotherly love"), eros, amor (p.120). Lover = "vividness, aliveness, and passion"; lives through primal hungers for sex, food, wellbeing, reproduction, creative adaptation, "and ultimately a sense of meaning" (p.120). Also the "sensation function": sensitivity to colours, sounds, textures, inner moods (p.120).
## Lover in his fullness (p.121-131)
- Archetype of play and "display", healthy embodiment, sensuous pleasure without shame (p.121).
- Connectedness: "the world in a grain of sand"; the boy who felt like an ant and the moss (p.121). Openness to a vast collective unconscious; "oceanic" connectedness (p.121-122).
- Passion through feeling, not intellect; wants to touch and be touched; recognises no boundaries; aesthetic consciousness (Kalahari nomads seeing hundreds of desert colours) (p.122).
- Source of spirituality and mysticism: intuits "the ultimate Oneness of all that is"; the boy at camp longing to fly into the night forest, "one with the Mystery" (p.124).
- Joy in senses: music, language learned by feeling, Whitehead's felt philosophy (p.124-125). Reads people; feels their pain too: Jesus weeping, "man of sorrows"; Paul: "love bears all things ... endures all things" (p.125).
- Opposes artificial boundaries; tension "amor and Roma", passion vs duty (Campbell) (p.125-126). Opposed at first glance to King, Warrior, Magician concerns for order and discipline (p.126).
- Cultural background (authors' view): they argue Christianity, Judaism and Islam as "moral, or ethical, religions" have "persecuted the Lover" while it returned through mysticism, hymns, the Song of Solomon (p.126-127). They describe Islam as "a religion of Warrior energy asceticism" with the Lover appearing in its depiction of paradise (p.127-128). Hinduism celebrates the erotic (Konarak) (p.128). (Authors' generalisations; contestable and worth discussing with the camp sheikhs rather than adopting.)
- Accountant's "Dream of the Indian Girl" reawakens his felt spirituality (p.128-129).
- Lover lives in artists and psychics, hunches, connoisseurs, buffs, the preacher "thinking with his heart", anyone who will "stop to smell the roses", and in falling in love (p.129-130).
- Monogamy arises from amor and inner rootedness; polygamy and harems also express the Lover (p.131).
## Shadow Lover (p.131-140)
- SHADOW Lover active: Addicted Lover. Key question: "Why should I put any limits on my sensual and sexual experience?" (p.131-132). LOSTNESS: pulled off centre by every impression, "the victim of his own sensitivity" (p.132). Examples: the oversensitive composer with notes everywhere; the Hebrew student absorbed into feeling; vintage cars to bankruptcy; artist spending the baby-formula money; the smoker who could not stop (p.132-133). "The sin of sensuality" (Niebuhr); maya (p.133). Can't step back from destructive relationships (p.133-135). Eternally restless: the cowboy riding into the sunset, James Bond, Don Juan (p.135). "Monogamy ... can be seen as the product of a man's own deep rootedness and centeredness. He is bounded, not by external rules but by his own inner structures" (p.135). Idolatry: investing fragments with the power of the Unity; pornography as fragmentation; seeking the endless "high" (p.135-136). "Boundary issues"; tidal wave dream: needs distance, detachment and heroic boundaries (p.137). Mishima burning the Golden Temple (p.138). Will lose jobs and marriage (p.138).
- SHADOW Lover passive: Impotent Lover. Flat affect, boredom, insomnia, monotone, alienation, "All is vanity" (Ecclesiastes): depression (p.138). Depression as a shield against "hot" feeling; dissociation (talking about oneself in the third person) (p.139). "without a vision, the people perish" (p.139). Sexual inactivity from boredom, anger, stress, money worries; may flip to the Addict and seek satisfaction outside the primary relationship (p.139-140).
## Accessing the Lover (p.140-141)
- Rightly accessed with strong Ego: "related, connected, alive, enthusiastic, compassionate, empathic, energized" (p.140). The Lover gives "a sense of meaning", spirituality, longing for a better world (p.140).
- King, Warrior and Magician need the Lover to humanise them and keep them from becoming sadistic; the Lover needs the King for limits, the Warrior to cut free decisively, the Magician to reflect (p.140-141).
- "The trouble with most of us is not that we feel too much passion, but that we don't feel our passion much at all." (p.141)

- "He becomes the victim of his own sensitivity." (p.132)
- "He is bounded, not by external rules but by his own inner structures" (p.135)

- "They need the Lover to keep them from becoming sadistic." (p.140)
- "The trouble with most of us is not that we feel too much passion, but that we don't feel our passion much at all." (p.141)
## Practices
- Stop and feel without performing ("stop to smell the roses") (p.130).
- Build boundaries via King/Warrior/Magician when lost in feeling (p.140-141).
- Notice depression as a shield over feeling (p.139).
## Camp link (interpretation)

# Conclusion: Accessing the Archetypal Powers of the Mature Masculine (p.143-156)
## Summary
- Lord of the Flies: humanity may always have lived under "the curse of infantilism"; patriarchy is really "puerarchy" (rule of boys) (p.143).
- Old structures (sacred kings, warrior cultures, magicians, honoured seers and poets) are gone; we must use inner resources as individuals (p.143-145).
- First step: "critical self-appraisal": ask how, not whether, shadows show up (p.145).
- "Humility is not humiliation." True humility = knowing our limitations and getting the help we need (p.145).
## Techniques (PRACTICE)
1. ACTIVE IMAGINATION DIALOGUE (p.145-151): the Ego converses with inner figures (complexes, archetype poles), ideally in writing, uncensored, labelling each voice. Treat it as a board meeting; at least "agree to disagree" or reach a truce. Paul: "Why do I do the things I don't want to do". Caution: if you meet a vicious "inner persecutor", stop and consult a therapist, or invoke a positive archetype first (p.147).
   - Example 1, Ego and Trickster: a man ridiculing his boss discovers the Trickster carries his suppressed feelings; they make a deal (attention, a holiday) and the persecutor becomes "a lifelong friend" (p.147-150). Inner figures "want to be noticed, honored, and taken seriously" (p.149).
   - Example 2, Ego referees Hero and Lover over girlfriend Gail's Brazil trip: "both right, but both excessive"; set limits and love at the same time (p.150-151).
2. INVOCATION (p.151-153): quiet place, relax, focus on an image with words (e.g. a king on a throne); call up the archetype; make the Ego his servant; ask for his help. Examples: praying to Eros before finding a wife (p.152-153); a crystal pyramid imagined in the chest to stay centred under attack (p.153). Authors compare it to prayer with ritual focus (p.153).
3. ADMIRING MEN (p.153-154): admire older men, living or dead; read biographies; target the archetype you lack (Warrior: Ramses II, Zulu chief, Patton; King: Lincoln; Lover: Leo Buscaglia) (p.154). "what images and thoughts we invoke determine to a large extent not only how things look to us but how they actually are" (p.154).
4. ACTING "AS IF" (p.154-155): method acting. Lover: really look at a sunset; Warrior: get off the couch, walk, take up a martial art, start on the unpaid bills; Magician: when asked for wisdom, listen fully and give it thoughtfully (p.155).
## A Final Word (p.155-156)
- Men should not apologise for their gender but steward it; "The enemy for both sexes is not the other sex but infantile grandiosity" (p.156).
- Transformation takes time and effort; do the conscious "homework" and the unconscious responds (p.156).
- "The struggle for maturity is a psychological, moral, and spiritual imperative from the Chinese Emperor within every man." (p.156)
## Selected readings (p.157-159)
Ardrey, Gilmore, Goodall, Turner; Eliade, Frazer; Jung (Campbell ed.), Edinger, Jacobi, Stevens; Campbell Hero with a Thousand Faces, Golding, Alice Miller; Bly Iron John, Bolen, Browning, Winnicott; Frankfort, Perry; Rogers, Stevens Roots of War; Butler, Neihardt, Nicolson; Neumann, Spink.
## Camp link (interpretation)
- Invocation and admiration map onto Islamic practice the camp already uses: dua, and studying the lives of the Prophet and Ahlul Bayt (e.g. Imam Ali as warrior-king-sage). This is my mapping, not the book's.
- Active imagination: good notebook exercise at camp (camp provides notebook).
- Acting as if: the camp's training and punctuality are "as if" Warrior practice.

# King Arthur: Legend of the Sword (2017): scene-by-scene plot
## Source
Wikipedia, "King Arthur: Legend of the Sword", Plot section, fetched 31 Oct 2026: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Arthur:_Legend_of_the_Sword . Scene grouping and numbering are mine; events are from that summary. Not watched by me. Camp copy: https://drive.proton.me/urls/JX6GD4KXGR#b98ZeiMdckhI
## Facts
Director Guy Ritchie; writers Joby Harold, Guy Ritchie, Lionel Wigram (story David Dobkin, Joby Harold); 126 min; released May 2017 (Wikipedia).
## Scenes
1. SCENE Siege of Camelot: opening caption: man and mage lived in peace until the mage Mordred turned on man. Mordred besieges Camelot; King Uther infiltrates his lair and beheads him with a sword forged by Merlin.
2. SCENE Vortigern's coup: Uther's brother Vortigern, coveting the throne, sacrifices his wife Elsa to the Syrens (sea witches) to become the Demon Knight, kills Queen Igraine and defeats Uther. Young Arthur escapes by boat to Londinium.
3. SCENE Street upbringing (montage): raised by prostitutes in a brothel, Arthur grows into a tough, street-smart minor chieftain. He has recurring nightmares of his parents' deaths without seeing the killer.
4. SCENE Vortigern's tower and the sword: Vortigern rules cruelly and builds a tower to grow his magical power. Receding waters reveal a sword in a stone; every man of age is brought to try it.
5. SCENE Pulling the sword: Arthur evades capture for a while, is caught, pulls the sword, and collapses from its power.
6. SCENE Vortigern's revelation: Vortigern tells the captive Arthur his lineage and the sword's meaning, and plans a public execution.
7. SCENE Rescue: a mage, an acolyte of Merlin, approaches Uther's former general Sir Bedivere. At the execution she creates a diversion and Bedivere's men rescue Arthur.
8. SCENE Refusal: at the hideout Arthur refuses to help; he does not believe he is king.
9. SCENE Darklands trial: Bedivere takes Arthur to the Darklands. He sees that the Demon Knight, Vortigern, killed his mother, and that his father sacrificed himself to save him, entombing the sword in stone made of his own body. Arthur accepts he is the rightful king. He learns Vortigern provoked Mordred's attack out of jealousy of Uther.
10. SCENE Insurgency: Arthur and the rebels chip away at Vortigern's army and try to assassinate him. The attempt fails; in the battle several men die, one is captured, and Arthur's friend Back Lack is killed by Vortigern. Arthur escapes with Back Lack's son Blue.
11. SCENE The lake: frustrated, Arthur tries to throw the sword into a lake. The Lady of the Lake returns it and shows him England's future under Vortigern. He accepts his responsibility.
12. SCENE Hideout lost: the captured rebel revealed the hideout under torture; the mage and Blue are taken and the other rebels killed. Vortigern demands Arthur's surrender.
13. SCENE Exchange: Bedivere hands over the sword for the mage; Arthur promises to surrender the next day for Blue. The mage protects Arthur with snake venom.
14. SCENE Castle confrontation: a giant snake controlled by the mage attacks the castle; Vortigern is protected by snake blood. Bedivere's rebels attack; Arthur retakes the sword and pursues Vortigern into the tower.
15. SCENE Final duel: Vortigern sacrifices his daughter Catia to become the Demon Knight again. In a brutal fight Arthur has a vision of his father passing Excalibur to him and defeats Vortigern. As Vortigern dies, Arthur consoles him.
16. SCENE Round Table: Arthur claims the throne, knights his friends and begins building the Round Table.
## Sourced quotes
- Opening caption: "For centuries man & mage lived side by side in peace until the rise of the mage sorcerer Mordred, turning his dark ambition against man, he marches on the last remaining stronghold...Camelot" (Wikipedia plot section)
- No dialogue quotes recorded; I could not verify any from a reputable source.
# Characters (source: Wikipedia cast list)
- Arthur (Charlie Hunnam): Uther's son, raised by prostitutes in Londinium, would-be king.
- Vortigern (Jude Law): Uther's brother, usurper, becomes the Demon Knight through sacrifices.
- Uther Pendragon (Eric Bana): Arthur's father, the previous king.
- The Mage (Astrid Berges-Frisbey): Merlin's acolyte; supports Arthur and the resistance. Originally written as Guinevere.
- Sir Bedivere (Djimon Hounsou): resistance leader, Uther's former knight.
- Goosefat Bill / Sir William (Aidan Gillen): archer, Uther's former knight.
- Back Lack (Neil Maskell): Arthur's childhood friend, Blue's father, killed by Vortigern.
- Wet Stick / Sir Tristan (Kingsley Ben-Adir): childhood friend.
- Blue (Bleu Landau): Back Lack's son.
- Kung Fu George / Sir George (Tom Wu): Arthur's martial arts teacher.
- Percy / Sir Percival (Craig McGinlay): friend.
- Rubio (Freddie Fox): rebel who reveals the hideout under torture.
- Maggie (Annabelle Wallis): in Vortigern's court, helps the resistance.
- Elsa (Katie McGrath): Vortigern's wife, sacrificed.
- Catia (Millie Brady): Vortigern's daughter, sacrificed.
- Igraine (Poppy Delevingne): Arthur's mother.
- Lady of the Lake (Jacqui Ainsley).
- Greybeard (Mikael Persbrandt): Viking dealing with Vortigern.
- Trigger (David Beckham): guard at the sword.
- Syrens (Lorraine Bruce, Eline Powell, Hermione Corfield).
# Reception and critics' themes (source: Wikipedia Critical response section)
- Rotten Tomatoes 31% (279 reviews, avg 4.7/10); Metacritic 41; CinemaScore B+.
- Peter Bradshaw, The Guardian: "a gonzo monarch, a death-metal warrior-king"; "often surprisingly entertaining".
- Matt Zoller Seitz, RogerEbert.com: 1.5/4; Ritchie rushes us so we "never have time to absorb any character or moment".
- Michael Phillips, Chicago Tribune: "a grim and stupid thing".
- Alissa Wilkinson, Vox: "surprisingly good, and surprisingly political" (read in light of Brexit).
- Box office about US$148.7m against a US$175m budget; planned six-film franchise cancelled.
## Themes named in sources
Origin story; rightful lineage vs usurper; Arthur "discovers his lineage" and "teams with a group of rebels to fight against the tyrannical king" (Wikipedia lead).
# Archetype and camp-theme mapping (MY OWN INTERPRETATION, not from any source)
Scene numbers refer to 01_plot_scenes.md; book refs to ../0X files.
## King
- Vortigern = SHADOW King Tyrant, "usurpation syndrome" (05, p.71): seizes the throne, sacrifices wife and daughter, builds a tower for his own power; like Herod and Saul he hunts the rightful heir (05, p.63-64). Scenes 2, 4, 15.
- Arthur refusing the crown = Weakling / "abdication syndrome" (05, p.71-72). Scene 8.
- Uther = generative King; passing the sword in the final vision = the father's blessing young men "starve" for (05, p.61). Scene 15.
- Round Table = King's ordering and blessing: knighting friends, seeing their worth (05, p.61). Scene 16.
- Arthur consoling the dying Vortigern = King compassion (Lover in the King). Scene 15. Interpretation.
## Warrior
- Street-fighter Arthur = Hero energy, skilled but serving himself (03, p.37-42). Scene 3.
- Trying to throw away the sword = loss of transpersonal commitment; Lady of the Lake restores the cause bigger than himself (06, p.84). Scene 11.
- Kung Fu George's training = Warrior training and skill (06, p.83). Scene 3.
- Vortigern's sacrifices = Sadist cruelty without passion (06, p.89).
## Magician
- The Mage = Magician as ritual elder/initiator, guiding Arthur through the Darklands (07, p.98). Scenes 7, 9, 13.
- Darklands = sacred space and initiatory ordeal; confronting the hidden trauma (01, p.6; 07, p.104). Scene 9.
- Vortigern's tower and Syrens = Shadow Magician, power without containment (07, p.111). Interpretation.
## Lover
- Arthur's loyalty to his street brothers and to Blue = connectedness (08, p.120 agape). Scenes 10, 12.
- Grief over Back Lack = Lover's capacity to feel pain (08, p.125).
## Initiation arc (01)
Boy (scene 3) -> ordeal (sword, Darklands, scenes 5, 9) -> death of the Hero (failure, loss of friends, scene 10-12) -> rebirth as King in service (scenes 15-16). Matches "The boy is dead and the man is born" (01, p.4-5).
## Camp themes
- Faith: Arthur's power fails while he fights alone; it returns when he accepts a calling beyond himself. Discussion: what is my "sword" (amanah, trust from Allah) that I try to put down?
- Discipline: the nightmares end only when he faces the memory. Discipline = facing what you avoid, not just training hard.
- Brotherhood: rebels from different backgrounds (a Chinese martial-arts master, Bedivere, street friends) form the Round Table. Parallel to the camp's 13 nationalities.
- Leadership as service: kingship given by lineage and blessing, not seized; Vortigern trades family for power. Parallel to the King's "steward" (05, p.70).
## Reflection questions
1. Where am I Vortigern (grasping control, sacrificing family for work or status)?
2. Where am I refusing the crown (Weakling), knowing a responsibility is mine?
3. What memory or "Darklands" have I avoided looking at?
4. Who are my Bedivere and my Mage (elders), and my Round Table (brothers)?
5. As a father of a newborn and Hassan, what sword am I passing on?

# Munajat Sha'baniyya: notes

## Context
- The Whispered Prayer of Sha'ban. Narrated by Ibn Khalawayh, who said it is the munajat of Imam Ali, Commander of the Faithful, and the Imams (peace be upon them), who recited it in the month of Sha'ban (per duas.org, which follows Shaykh Abbas Qummi's Mafatih al-Jinan; also reported by Ibn Tawus in Iqbal al-A'mal and al-Kaf'ami).
- Recommended in Sha'ban but suitable at any time, with presence of heart.
- Mirza Javad Agha Maliki Tabrizi, a teacher of Imam Khomeini in ethics, said it holds a wealth of knowledge on the manners of beseeching Allah. Imam Khomeini often quoted it, especially segments 104 to 108.
- Length: 134 short segments, about 10 to 15 minutes recited slowly.

## Key themes
1. Standing before Allah, fully known (1 to 20): nothing hidden, everything in His hand.
2. Confession as the means of approach (29 to 33): admitting the sin is itself the way in.
3. Hope greater than deeds (44 to 63): "if You seize me for my crime, I will hold on to Your pardon".
4. Love even in the Fire (59): love of Allah as unconditional loyalty.
5. Wasted youth and awakening (64 to 77): strength to turn comes only when He wakes us to His love.
6. Heart, tongue and gaze (82 to 84): longing, truthfulness, true seeing.
7. Detachment and the veils of light (104 to 108): the summit of the prayer.
8. Secret intimacy, open action (111): He speaks in private, the servant works in public.
9. Covenant and watchfulness (124 to 131): constant remembrance, keeping the covenant, awe and self-watching (muraqaba).

## Segments with uncertain or debated meaning
- 66: 'ightirari bika': being deluded or over-confident about You (taking Your forbearance for granted). Some render it 'my being deceived concerning You'.
- 80: 'al-mughtarr bihi': the one who is deluded about Him, ie heedlessly presumes on His forbearance. The duas.org 'those who love Him ardently' is not supported by the Arabic.
- 87: 'ghayr mamlul': never grown weary of, ie God does not tire of him. duas.org's 'servility' is a mistranslation.
- 94: 'walahan bi-dhikrika ila dhikrika': ardent love through Your remembrance towards (further) remembrance. The 'ila dhikrika' is read variously.
- 95: 'rawh najah asma'ika': literally 'the refreshment of the success of Your names'. Meaning is debated; rendered as the joy of success in (attaining) Your names.
- 104: 'kamal al-inqita' ilayk': complete cutting off (from all else) towards You. A technical spiritual term; rendered by paraphrase.

## Reflection prompts (mine, written for camp prep, not from the camp)
1. Segment 5, "I have fled to You": what are you running from, and what are you running towards, in coming to this camp?
2. Segment 31 makes confession the way in. What is one honest admission you could bring to Salat al-Layl this week?
3. Segments 64 and 65 talk about youth spent in heedlessness. As a new father, what do you want Hassan to see in you that you did not have at his age?
4. Segment 73: strength to change came only when He woke you. When have you been woken, and what did you do with it?
5. Segments 82 to 84 ask for a heart, tongue and gaze. Which of the three needs the most training before 30 Nov?
6. Segment 111: secret intimacy, open action. How does the Warrior's discipline on the mat connect to what happens in your prayer at night?
7. Segment 125, not breaking the covenant: what commitment will you make at camp, and how will you keep it back home with Zainab and the family?
8. Segment 127, never taking His command lightly: where do you currently take it lightly?
9. Segment 104, complete detachment: what one attachment will you deliberately leave behind for the week of camp?
10. Segment 131, awe and watchfulness: what would a daily muraqaba check (two minutes before sleep) look like for you?
